description: Swap the RandomForestRegressor for lightgbm.LGBMRegressor (300 estimators, learning_rate 0.1, random_state=seed) on the same Morgan fingerprints.

Replace the random forest with XGBRegressor trained with early_stopping_rounds=50 on a random 10% validation split carved from the training molecules, keeping the same features.

issues: No sign of gaming the measurement. The diff only swaps RandomForestRegressor for XGBRegressor. It reads no files, pastes in no labels and never touches test labels. It still passes the seed through random_state and stays within the 8 threads.
No bug that would make the result meaningless. fit_predict still trains only on train_smiles/train_y and returns one prediction per test molecule.

Minor cleanup: MAX_FEATURES and MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF are no longer used and should be deleted. N_TREES now sets the number of XGBoost boosting rounds (at learning_rate 0.05), not the forest size, so the old name and value may not suit XGBoost.

Recomputed z: the candidate improves on the incumbent by 0.3911 - 0.3901 = 0.0010. With one run on each side and a noise sd of 0.0037, the sd of the difference is 0.0037*sqrt(2) ≈ 0.00523, so z ≈ 0.19. That matches the reported 0.183 once rounding of the values is allowed for. The gain is well within noise, so the provisional reject is consistent with the numbers. The diff makes no claims to check.

description: Replace the RandomForestRegressor with XGBRegressor using subsample=0.8 and colsample_bytree=0.8 on the existing fingerprint-plus-descriptor features, to add row and column stochasticity as a regularizer.

Append degree-2 interaction-only PolynomialFeatures products of the 8 RDKit descriptor columns (TPSA, MolWt, MolLogP, HBD, HBA, Chi1n, Kappa2, BertzCT) to the Morgan fingerprint matrix, leaving featurize and the random forest otherwise unchanged.

Replace the random forest with xgb.XGBRegressor (learning_rate=0.05, max_depth=6, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.8, up to 1000 trees, early_stopping_rounds=50), keeping the fingerprint and RDKit descriptor features, with early stopping driven by a seed-based 1/6 validation split of the training data so the test molecules are never used for stopping.

Stack RandomForest, XGBoost and CatBoost base models, using 5-fold out-of-fold predictions as the inputs to a 50-tree random-forest meta-regressor, to test whether combining the three learners beats the single random forest on the descriptor-augmented features.
Change the Morgan fingerprint radius from 2 to 3 so the RF sees larger substructure context, leaving everything else (RF model and appended RDKit descriptors) unchanged.

Extends the RDKit descriptor block appended to the Morgan fingerprints with rotatable bonds, fraction Csp3, and heavy-atom count, keeping the 8 existing descriptors; CalcTotalMolLogP is skipped because it is not an rdMolDescriptors function and duplicates MolLogP.

Add RDKit count features (atom count, heavy-atom count, rotatable-bond count) to the existing RDKit descriptor block appended to the Morgan fingerprints, skipping the spec's MolWt/HBD/HBA entries that are already present.

Proposed swapping the RandomForestRegressor for xgboost.XGBRegressor (learning_rate=0.1, max_depth=6, n_estimators=300, n_jobs=-1, random_state=seed), but I am aborting this slot instead of running it.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The diff only swaps RandomForestRegressor for LGBMRegressor. It adds no file or network access, pasted answers or use of test labels. Randomness uses the seed argument and n_jobs=8 is within the limit.
No bug that would make the result meaningless. fit_predict still fits only on train_smiles/train_y and returns one prediction per test molecule.

Minor cleanup: MAX_FEATURES and MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF are no longer used by the model, and N_TREES now means LightGBM boosting rounds at learning_rate=0.05. That may be too few rounds for a fair test of LightGBM, but it does not invalidate the run.

Recomputed z: the candidate (0.3991) is 0.0080 worse than the incumbent (0.3911). Using the noise sd of 0.0037 for each single run, the sd of the difference is 0.0037*sqrt(2) = 0.00523, so z = -1.53. The harness's -1.513 matches once rounding of the reported means is allowed for.
Each side has only one run, but the candidate is worse, so the reject decision holds and no replicate is needed.

description: Replace the RandomForestRegressor with LGBMRegressor using subsample=0.8 (with subsample_freq=1 so it takes effect) and colsample_bytree=0.8, keeping the existing Morgan and RDKit descriptor features.

Swap the RandomForestRegressor for sklearn's ExtraTreesRegressor (same tree count, max_features and leaf size) to test whether the extra split randomness reduces overfitting on the descriptor-augmented fingerprints.
Raise the random forest's MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF from 1 to 2 so each leaf averages at least two training molecules, which may reduce overfitting to individual noisy labels.
Increase the random forest to 1000 trees and lower max_features from 0.3 to 0.1 so each split considers fewer features, for more diverse trees.

Abort: this idea (1000 trees with MAX_FEATURES=0.1 on the current descriptor-augmented RF) was already tested in slot 17 and rejected at 0.3961, which is worse than the incumbent 0.3911 by more than the noise.

Replace the random forest with XGBRegressor using a Huber-type robust objective (reg:pseudohubererror, huber_slope=1.0; the spec's 'reg:huber' is not an XGBoost objective name) on the existing Morgan and descriptor features, to test whether outlier-robust loss helps under the MAE metric.

Replace the random forest with an average of three XGBRegressor models that differ only in random_state (seed*3+k), to test whether seed-averaged boosting beats the single RF on the descriptor-augmented features.
Quantile Regression Forest approximation: predict the median of the per-tree RF predictions instead of their mean, which may suit the MAE objective.

issues: Integrity: no problems found. The change only replaces the forest's mean prediction with the median of the per-tree predictions on test_smiles. There is no file or network access, test labels are not used, and the trees keep the seeded random_state.

Correctness: estimators_ are DecisionTreeRegressors fitted on the same feature matrix, so tree.predict(featurize(test_smiles)) is valid. Because predictions are now built one tree at a time, the forest's n_jobs no longer applies to them, so prediction is a bit slower. That has no effect on correctness and won't come near the 10-minute limit.

Numbers: I recomputed z from the inputs. The candidate mean is (0.3861+0.3794)/2 = 0.38275, and its difference from the incumbent is 0.3911 - 0.38275 = 0.00835. The standard error is 0.0037*sqrt(1/2+1/1) = 0.00453, which gives z = 1.84. The harness reports 1.823, a small gap probably due to rounding or unrounded inputs, and it doesn't change the decision.

Borderline: the incumbent has only 1 run and the candidate 2. The gain is about 0.008 at z of about 1.8, so it's suggestive but not strong. The two candidate runs differ by 0.0067, which is within noise for a difference of two runs (sd about 0.0052). The edit is a simple, reasonable way to make the forest less sensitive to outliers. Accepting is defensible; a replicate of the incumbent would make the decision firmer.

Lower the random forest's MAX_FEATURES from 0.3 to 0.1 so each split considers a more diverse random subset of the Morgan and descriptor features.
Raise the random forest from 300 to 1000 trees (N_TREES) to reduce variance in the per-tree median prediction, keeping all other settings fixed; runtime should stay well within the 10-minute limit.
Scale the featurized inputs with sklearn MaxAbsScaler before the random forest; aborted because it cannot change the predictions.

Add a max_depth=15 cap to the random forest's trees (via a new MAX_DEPTH setting) to limit overfitting on this small dataset.

Target smoothing (moving average or Gaussian noise on train_y) was considered and aborted without a slot, because a moving average has no meaningful ordering over unordered molecules and Gaussian label noise is unlikely to beat the incumbent.

Replace the random forest with a simple average of three XGBRegressor models that differ only in random seed (seed, seed+1, seed+2), to test whether a seed-averaged boosting ensemble beats the current median-of-trees RF on the descriptor-augmented features.

Skip the StandardScaler-on-descriptors edit: a random forest splits each feature on thresholds only, so a per-feature affine rescale leaves the trees unchanged and the job would just reproduce the incumbent.

issues: No integrity problems. The diff only changes RADIUS from 2 to 1. Radius 1 is a valid setting for Morgan fingerprints. The diff adds no file access, no hardcoded answers and no use of test labels.
No bug makes the result meaningless. Radius 1 gives fewer distinct bit patterns, but the fingerprint and model code still work.

Recomputed z: (0.3828 - 0.3822) / (0.0037 * sqrt(1 + 1/2)) = 0.0006 / 0.00453 = 0.132. The harness reports 0.126. The gap is within the rounding of the 4-decimal values shown (a true difference of about 0.00057 gives 0.126), so the numbers agree.

The gain of 0.0006 is far below the noise (sd 0.0037), so reject is correct. One could argue radius 1 is the simpler setting and it ties the incumbent, but the evidence for any improvement is negligible.

description: Change the Morgan fingerprint radius from 2 to 1 so the random forest sees only immediate-neighbour atom environments, to test whether lower dimensionality generalises better to unseen scaffolds.

Abort: changing the Morgan radius from 2 to 1 was already tested in slot 32 (0.3822 vs incumbent 0.3828, delta -0.0006, inside the 0.0037 noise), so re-running it would only repeat a known result.
